items.definition: The five transport modes are air, ocean (sea), road, rail and pipeline; freight logistics mostly uses the first four, often combined.
items.definition_ar: وسائل النقل الخمس هي الجوي والبحري والبري والسكك الحديدية وخطوط الأنابيب، والشحن يستخدم غالبًا الأربعة الأولى وكثيرًا ما يجمع بينها.
items.explanation: They trade speed against cost and capacity. Air is fastest and most expensive per kilogram, suited to urgent, light or high-value goods (a breakdown part for a mine). Ocean is slowest and cheapest per tonne, suited to heavy and bulky goods (machines). Road gives door-to-door flexibility and dominates short distances and the first and last mile. Rail suits heavy volumes over long inland corridors where the network exists.
items.example: A grounded excavator's hydraulic pump goes by air; ten new excavators go by sea (RoRo or flat rack).

items.definition: Air freight is cargo carried by aircraft, in the holds of passenger flights (belly cargo) or on freighters, documented by an air waybill.
items.definition_ar: الشحن الجوي هو نقل البضائع بالطائرات، في عنابر طائرات الركاب أو على طائرات الشحن، ويُوثق ببوليصة الشحن الجوي.
items.explanation: Air cargo is charged on chargeable weight (the greater of actual and volumetric weight). It moves through the airline's cargo terminal at origin and destination, and its status events (received, departed, arrived, ready for collection) are per station, so an 'arrived' at a transit airport is not arrival at destination.

items.definition: Ocean freight is cargo carried by ship — containerised (FCL or LCL), roll-on/roll-off, break bulk or bulk — documented by a bill of lading or sea waybill.
items.definition_ar: الشحن البحري هو نقل البضائع بالسفن، في حاويات (كاملة أو مجمعة) أو دحرجة (RoRo) أو بضائع عامة أو صب، ويُوثق ببوليصة الشحن البحري.
items.explanation: Container lines run fixed services (rotations) with weekly sailings; transshipment at hub ports is common for African destinations, so delays often come from a missed connection rather than the first voyage.

items.definition: Road freight is cargo moved by truck, as a full truckload (FTL) or less than truckload (LTL); the cross-border road document is commonly the CMR consignment note.
items.definition_ar: النقل البري هو نقل البضائع بالشاحنات، حمولة كاملة (FTL) أو جزئية (LTL)، ومستند النقل البري الدولي الشائع هو إشعار CMR.
items.explanation: Road is the first and last mile of almost every shipment and the main inland mode in much of Africa; border crossings and transit regimes often dominate its transit time.

items.definition: Rail freight moves cargo by train — containers, wagonloads or block trains — economical for heavy volumes over long distances where the network and terminals exist.
items.definition_ar: النقل بالسكك الحديدية ينقل البضائع بالقطارات (حاويات أو عربات أو قطارات كاملة)، وهو اقتصادي للأحجام الكبيرة لمسافات طويلة حيث تتوفر الشبكة والمحطات.

items.definition: Multimodal transport carries goods by at least two modes under one contract and one transport document, with one operator responsible end to end. Intermodal usually means the goods stay in the same unit (a container) across modes.
items.definition_ar: النقل متعدد الوسائط ينقل البضاعة بوسيلتين أو أكثر بعقد ومستند واحد ومسؤولية مشغل واحد من البداية للنهاية، أما Intermodal فيعني غالبًا بقاء البضاعة في نفس الوحدة (الحاوية) عبر الوسائل.
items.explanation: Several separate contracts (sea with the line, then a separate truck) are segmented transport, not multimodal: each leg has its own carrier and liability.

items.definition: FCL is a shipment that uses a whole container for one shipper; the container is packed and sealed at origin and normally opened only at destination (or for inspection).
items.definition_ar: الحاوية الكاملة (FCL) شحنة تستخدم حاوية بالكامل لشاحن واحد، تُعبأ وتُختم في المنشأ ولا تُفتح عادة إلا في الوجهة أو للتفتيش.
items.explanation: FCL is usually cheaper per cubic metre than LCL once a container is more than roughly half full, and faster because there is no consolidation or deconsolidation. Free time, demurrage and detention apply to the container.

items.definition: LCL is a shipment too small for its own container; a consolidator groups several shippers' cargo into one container and separates it again at destination.
items.definition_ar: الشحنة المجمعة (LCL) أصغر من أن تملأ حاوية، فيجمعها المجمّع مع شحنات أخرى في حاوية واحدة ثم يفرزها في الوجهة.
items.explanation: LCL is charged per cubic metre or tonne (revenue ton) and takes longer: cargo waits for consolidation and deconsolidation at a CFS (container freight station). One shipper's missing document can hold the whole container at customs.
misconceptions: LCL is not always cheaper: handling charges at both ends can exceed the freight saving.

items.definition: The common ISO freight containers are the 20ft and 40ft general-purpose (dry) boxes, the 40ft high cube (about 30 cm taller), refrigerated (reefer), open top (loaded from above) and flat rack (no sides, for oversized cargo).
items.definition_ar: أشهر الحاويات القياسية: الحاوية الجافة 20 و40 قدم، والـ 40 قدم العالية (High Cube)، والمبردة (Reefer)، والمفتوحة من أعلى (Open Top)، والمسطحة (Flat Rack) للبضائع الكبيرة.
items.explanation: Machines wider or taller than a box go on flat racks or open tops, which are scarcer and often carry out-of-gauge surcharges. Exact dimensions and ratings are in ISO 668; check the line's equipment specification for a booking.
items.example: A dismantled excavator boom shipped on a 40ft flat rack.

sources.note: Not confirmed reachable from the verification host; dimensions are deliberately not stated here.

items.definition: A TEU is the capacity unit of container shipping: one 20ft container is 1 TEU, a 40ft is 2 TEU (one FEU).
items.definition_ar: الـ TEU وحدة سعة الشحن بالحاويات: الحاوية 20 قدمًا = 1 TEU، والحاوية 40 قدمًا = 2 TEU.

items.definition: Palletisation is building cargo onto pallets so it can be handled by forklift as one unit, protected and counted easily.
items.definition_ar: التحميل على المنصات هو تجميع البضاعة على منصات (بالتات) لتُنقل كوحدة واحدة بالرافعة الشوكية وتكون محمية وسهلة العد.
items.explanation: Wooden pallets crossing borders generally need ISPM 15 heat treatment and marking; check the destination's plant-health rules.

items.definition: A ULD is an aircraft container or pallet that lets air cargo be loaded as units that fit the aircraft's hold.
items.definition_ar: وحدة التحميل (ULD) حاوية أو منصة طائرة تسمح بتحميل الشحن الجوي كوحدات تناسب عنبر الطائرة.

items.definition: Chargeable weight is the weight a carrier bills: the greater of the actual gross weight and the volumetric weight calculated from the dimensions.
items.definition_ar: الوزن المحاسب هو الوزن الذي يحاسب عليه الناقل: الأكبر بين الوزن الفعلي الإجمالي والوزن الحجمي المحسوب من الأبعاد.
items.explanation: For air cargo the common convention is volumetric kg = length × width × height in cm ÷ 6000; courier products often use ÷ 5000. The divisor is the carrier's or contract's, so check it before calculating.
items.example: A crate 120 × 100 × 100 cm weighing 150 kg: 1,200,000 ÷ 6000 = 200 kg volumetric, so 200 kg is charged.
limitations: Divisors differ by carrier and product; ATLAS's calculator takes the divisor as an input.

items.definition: Transit time is how long the goods take to travel between two points — usually from departure (or pickup) at origin to arrival (or delivery) at destination.
items.definition_ar: زمن العبور هو المدة التي تستغرقها البضاعة للانتقال بين نقطتين، عادة من المغادرة أو الاستلام في المنشأ حتى الوصول أو التسليم في الوجهة.
items.explanation: Always say which two events are measured: port-to-port and door-to-door transit can differ by weeks. A carrier's published transit time is a schedule, not a promise, and transshipment connections add variance.

items.definition: Lead time is the total time from placing an order to having the goods available: supplier processing and production, pickup, transit, clearance and delivery.
items.definition_ar: زمن التوريد هو المدة الكلية من إصدار الطلب حتى توفر البضاعة: تجهيز المورد والتصنيع والاستلام والنقل والتخليص والتسليم.
items.explanation: Transit time is one part of lead time. Customs clearance in many African ports can be longer than the voyage itself, which is why clearance steps are tracked separately.
misconceptions: Lead time is not the same as transit time.

items.definition: A cut-off is the latest time cargo, documents or data must reach the carrier to make a sailing or flight: the container-yard (CY) cut-off, the documentation (SI) cut-off, the VGM cut-off; for air, the latest acceptance time (LAT).
items.definition_ar: الـ Cut-off هو آخر موعد يجب أن تصل فيه البضاعة أو المستندات أو البيانات للناقل للحاق بالرحلة: موعد ساحة الحاويات، وموعد المستندات، وموعد الوزن المعتمد VGM، وفي الجوي آخر موعد للقبول LAT.
items.explanation: Missing any cut-off typically rolls the cargo to the next sailing, moving the ETA by the service's frequency (often a week). 'Delivered before LAT' on an airline page means the shipper met the acceptance time — not that the cargo was delivered.

items.definition: Routing is the path and sequence of carriers, ports, airports and modes a shipment takes from origin to destination.
items.definition_ar: التوجيه هو المسار وتسلسل الناقلين والموانئ والمطارات ووسائل النقل التي تمر بها الشحنة من المنشأ إلى الوجهة.
items.explanation: A direct route has fewer handovers and less variance; a transshipment route may be cheaper or have more frequent departures but adds connection risk. Routing guides fix the preferred carriers and routes per lane.

items.definition: Transshipment is when cargo is unloaded from one vessel at an intermediate port and loaded onto another vessel to continue to its destination — typical at hub ports where a mainline service connects to a feeder.
items.definition_ar: المسافنة هي تفريغ البضاعة من سفينة في ميناء وسيط وتحميلها على سفينة أخرى لتكمل إلى وجهتها، وهي شائعة في موانئ المحاور حيث يتصل الخط الرئيسي بسفينة مغذية.
items.explanation: It adds a connection that can slip: if the second vessel is missed or delayed, the ETA moves even though the first leg ran on time. In air freight the same idea is a transit airport, and an 'arrived' there is not arrival at destination.

items.definition: A feeder is a smaller vessel that carries containers between a hub port and smaller ports the mainline ships do not call at — the second leg of a transshipment.
items.definition_ar: السفينة المغذية سفينة أصغر تنقل الحاويات بين ميناء محوري وموانئ أصغر لا تتوقف فيها السفن الرئيسية، وهي الرحلة الثانية في المسافنة.

items.definition: A blank sailing is a scheduled voyage the carrier cancels — the vessel skips a port or the whole rotation for that week.
items.definition_ar: الـ Blank sailing رحلة مجدولة يلغيها الناقل، فتتخطى السفينة ميناء أو الدورة كاملة في ذلك الأسبوع.
items.explanation: Carriers do it to manage capacity or recover schedules. Cargo booked on it is rolled to the next available sailing, so its ETA moves by roughly the service's frequency (often a week).

items.definition: Cargo is 'rolled' when it was booked on a sailing but is moved to a later one — because the vessel was full, the sailing was blanked, or the cargo missed the cut-off.
items.definition_ar: يُقال إن البضاعة رُحِّلت (Rolled) عندما تُنقل من الرحلة المحجوزة إلى رحلة لاحقة بسبب امتلاء السفينة أو إلغاء الرحلة أو فوات الموعد النهائي.
items.explanation: The ETA moves accordingly. A sudden ETA jump of about a week on an ocean shipment is a typical sign; confirm with the carrier's booking or vessel details rather than assuming.

items.definition: Port congestion is when vessels have to wait at anchor because berths or yard capacity are full.
items.definition_ar: ازدحام الموانئ هو انتظار السفن عند المخطاف لأن الأرصفة أو الساحات ممتلئة.
items.explanation: Waiting time adds directly to arrival and discharge, so ETAs slip; it also slows container availability after discharge and can push containers into demurrage.

items.definition: The usual reasons are port congestion (waiting for a berth), weather, missed or delayed transshipment connections, blank sailings and schedule recovery, canal or strait disruptions, equipment or crew issues, and slow-steaming to save fuel.
items.definition_ar: الأسباب المعتادة: ازدحام الموانئ، والطقس، وفوات أو تأخر رحلات المسافنة، وإلغاء الرحلات وإعادة ضبط الجداول، واضطرابات القنوات والمضائق، ومشكلات المعدات أو الطاقم، والإبحار البطيء لتوفير الوقود.
items.explanation: The carrier's schedule updates and port notices usually say which applies. Without them, a cause is a hypothesis, not a finding.

items.definition: A voyage number identifies one specific sailing of a vessel on a service; the IMO number is a permanent 7-digit identifier assigned to a seagoing ship.
items.definition_ar: رقم الرحلة يحدد إبحارًا معينًا لسفينة على خدمة ما، ورقم IMO معرف دائم من سبعة أرقام يُعطى للسفينة.
items.explanation: The IMO number stays the same when the ship is renamed or changes owner, so it is the reliable way to identify a vessel. The same vessel makes many voyages; the vessel name plus voyage number pins down the sailing your cargo is on.

items.definition: Carrier selection is choosing which carrier (and service) to use on a lane by comparing price, transit time, reliability, capacity, coverage, tracking quality and claims handling.
items.definition_ar: اختيار الناقل هو تحديد الناقل والخدمة على مسار معين بمقارنة السعر وزمن العبور والموثوقية والسعة والتغطية وجودة التتبع ومعالجة المطالبات.
items.explanation: Compare like with like: the same lane, mode and period. A carrier with a lower average transit time on easy lanes is not better than one that serves the hard lanes. Schedule reliability often matters more than the fastest published transit time.

items.definition: A freight rate is the base charge for carriage plus surcharges and local charges; it can be a contract rate (fixed for a period) or a spot rate (market price for one shipment).
items.definition_ar: سعر الشحن هو الأجرة الأساسية للنقل مضافًا إليها الرسوم الإضافية والمحلية، وقد يكون سعر تعاقد ثابت لفترة أو سعرًا فوريًا لشحنة واحدة.
items.explanation: Compare quotes on an all-in basis (base + surcharges + origin and destination charges) for the same scope; a low base rate with high surcharges is common. Air rates are per chargeable kg in weight breaks; ocean FCL per container; LCL per revenue ton.

items.definition: Surcharges are charges added to the base freight: fuel (BAF in ocean, fuel surcharge in air), currency (CAF), peak season (PSS), general rate increases (GRI), security and war risk, and terminal handling charges (THC) at each end.
items.definition_ar: الرسوم الإضافية تُضاف إلى أجرة الشحن الأساسية: الوقود (BAF)، فروق العملة (CAF)، موسم الذروة (PSS)، الزيادات العامة (GRI)، الأمن ومخاطر الحرب، ورسوم المناولة في المحطات (THC).
items.explanation: Who pays each charge follows the Incoterms rule and the contract: under FOB the destination THC is usually the buyer's, origin THC the seller's. Surcharge names and amounts are the carrier's and change often; read the quote.

items.definition: Capacity constraints are limits on space or equipment — vessel slots, empty containers, aircraft payload, trucks, port or warehouse capacity — that delay or price up shipments when demand exceeds them.
items.definition_ar: قيود السعة هي حدود المساحة أو المعدات (مساحات السفن، الحاويات الفارغة، حمولة الطائرات، الشاحنات، طاقة الموانئ والمخازن) التي تؤخر الشحنات أو ترفع أسعارها عندما يتجاوز الطلب السعة.
items.explanation: Under constraint, carriers prioritise contract and premium cargo, roll lower-priority bookings and add surcharges; booking earlier and having alternatives are the usual mitigations.

items.definition: Under the SOLAS convention a packed export container's verified gross mass must be provided by the shipper to the carrier and terminal before it is loaded; without it the container is not loaded.
items.definition_ar: وفق اتفاقية سولاس يجب أن يقدم الشاحن الوزن الإجمالي المعتمد (VGM) للحاوية المعبأة إلى الناقل والمحطة قبل تحميلها، وبدونه لا تُحمّل الحاوية.
items.explanation: The requirement has applied since 1 July 2016. A missing or late VGM is a common reason a box misses its vessel.

items.definition: Cross-docking moves incoming goods straight to outgoing transport with little or no storage in between.
items.definition_ar: التحويل المباشر (Cross-docking) نقل البضائع الواردة مباشرة إلى وسيلة النقل الصادرة دون تخزين أو بتخزين قصير جدًا.

items.definition: A master air waybill (MAWB) is issued by the airline to the forwarder for a consolidated shipment; each shipper's goods inside it travel on a house air waybill (HAWB) issued by the forwarder.
items.explanation: Airlines track by the MAWB number (an airline prefix and serial); a forwarder's portal tracks by the HAWB. When an airline site shows a status the forwarder's does not, check which number each is reading.

items.definition: Consolidation is a forwarder combining several shippers' smaller shipments into one larger shipment under one master transport document, to buy capacity at a lower rate.
items.explanation: LCL in ocean and consolidated air cargo work this way. Each shipment keeps its own house document, and a delay or hold on the consolidation affects every shipment in it.

items.definition: A full truckload (FTL) uses a whole truck for one shipper's goods; less-than-truckload (LTL) shares a truck with other shippers' goods and is charged for the space or weight used.
items.explanation: FTL is faster and handles goods less; LTL is cheaper for small volumes but goes through hubs, adding transit time and handling risk.

items.definition: A CMR consignment note is the standard transport document for international carriage of goods by road between countries party to the CMR Convention; it evidences the contract of carriage.
items.explanation: Unlike an ocean bill of lading it is not a document of title. The convention also sets the carrier's liability rules for international road carriage between its contracting parties.
limitations: The CMR Convention applies only between countries that are party to it; whether a given road leg is covered depends on the countries involved.

items.term: Terminal handling and bunker charges (THC, BAF)
items.definition: Terminal handling charges (THC) cover handling a container at the terminal at origin or destination; the bunker adjustment factor (BAF) is a fuel surcharge that changes with fuel prices.
items.explanation: They are billed on top of the base ocean rate, and who pays origin and destination THC depends on the Incoterms rule and the contract. Unexpected 'destination THC' on a CIF purchase is a common dispute.

items.definition: Freight audit is checking carrier and forwarder invoices against the agreed rates, the booking and the services actually performed before paying them.
items.explanation: Typical findings: wrong weight or chargeable weight, a surcharge not in the agreement, duplicate invoices, demurrage charged for days already covered by free time.

items.definition: A cargo claim is a demand to the carrier (or forwarder) for compensation for goods lost, damaged or delayed in its care.
items.explanation: Note the damage on the delivery receipt or POD at delivery, keep photos and the packaging, and give written notice quickly. The time limits and the carrier's liability limit come from the applicable convention and the contract, and differ by mode — check them before relying on any figure.
limitations: Notice periods and liability limits differ by mode and convention; ATLAS does not state them without the governing document.

items.definition: A delivery order (DO) is the instruction issued by the carrier or its agent, after the freight is settled and the bill of lading surrendered (or released), allowing the consignee to collect the cargo from the terminal.
items.explanation: No delivery order, no gate-out — even after customs release. A delayed DO, often from unpaid charges or a missing original B/L, is a common cause of demurrage.

items.definition: Gate-in is a container entering a terminal or depot; gate-out is it leaving.
items.explanation: At origin, gate-in of the full container precedes loading; at destination, the full gate-out ends demurrage and starts detention, and the empty gate-in (return) ends detention.

items.definition: Schedule reliability is the share of vessel (or flight) arrivals that happen on the scheduled day or within an agreed window.
items.explanation: Low schedule reliability means the published ETA is a weak predictor; plan with buffer and track the vessel, not the schedule.
